28def nextafter_func(input, other): 

29 # IEEE 754 nextafter: returns the next representable float after input towards other 

30 # For float16/bfloat16: use bit manipulation on the uint16 representation to 

31 # compute the next value in the native precision. Computing in float32 then 

32 # casting back would silently skip intermediate fp16/bf16 values because the 

33 # float32 next value may round to the same lower-precision value (e.g. 

34 # nextafter(1., 2.) in fp16 is 1.0009765625, but the fp32 next value 

35 # 1.00000012 rounds back to 1.0 in fp16). 

36 # For float32: use libdevice's nextafter (which also handles NaN / Inf / same). 

37 dtype = input.dtype 

38 if tl.constexpr(dtype == tl.float16) or tl.constexpr(dtype == tl.bfloat16): 

39 # NaN check: all exponent bits set and mantissa non-zero 

40 if tl.constexpr(dtype == tl.float16): 

41 exp_mask: tl.constexpr = 0x7C00 # 5 exponent bits 

42 frac_mask: tl.constexpr = 0x03FF # 10 mantissa bits 

43 else: # bf16 

44 exp_mask: tl.constexpr = 0x7F80 # 8 exponent bits 

45 frac_mask: tl.constexpr = 0x007F # 7 mantissa bits 

46 

47 x_int = input.to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True) 

48 y_int = other.to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True) 

49 

50 # NaN: all exponent bits set and mantissa non-zero 

51 x_is_nan = ((x_int & exp_mask) == exp_mask) & ((x_int & frac_mask) != 0) 

52 y_is_nan = ((y_int & exp_mask) == exp_mask) & ((y_int & frac_mask) != 0) 

53 is_nan = x_is_nan | y_is_nan 

54 

55 # Same value: return input (matches IEEE 754) 

56 is_equal = input == other 

57 

58 sign_bit = 0x8000 

59 is_positive = (x_int & sign_bit) == 0 

60 is_going_up = input < other 

61 

62 # --- uint16 constants via bitwise ops (arithmetic on uint16 + Python int 

63 # would promote to int32, breaking the final bitcast) --- 

64 uint_zero = x_int & 0 # uint16(0) 

65 uint_one = uint_zero | 1 # uint16(1) 

66 uint_neg_one = ~uint_zero # uint16(0xFFFF) = -1 in uint16 arithmetic 

67 cross_const = uint_zero | 0x8001 # uint16(0x8001) 

68 

69 # Manipulate the unsigned integer representation. 

70 # IEEE 754 sign-magnitude means that for positive numbers a larger 

71 # uint corresponds to a larger float value, while for negative numbers 

72 # a larger uint corresponds to a more-negative (smaller) float value. 

73 # 

74 # Normal increment: 

75 # positive going up: x_int + 1 

76 # positive going down: x_int - 1 (= x_int + 0xFFFF in uint16) 

77 # negative going up: x_int - 1 (less negative) 

78 # negative going down: x_int + 1 (more negative) 

79 normal_inc = tl.where( 

80 is_positive, 

81 tl.where(is_going_up, uint_one, uint_neg_one), 

82 tl.where(is_going_up, uint_neg_one, uint_one), 

83 ) 

84 

85 # Zero-crossing needs special handling: 

86 # +0 going down: 0x0000 should become 0x8001 (largest negative subnormal) 

87 # -0 going up: 0x8000 should become 0x0001 (smallest positive subnormal) 

88 # In both cases x_int + 0x8001 gives the correct result in uint16: 

89 # 0x0000 + 0x8001 = 0x8001 (target) 

90 # 0x8000 + 0x8001 = 0x0001 (wraps around in uint16) 

91 pos_zero_down = is_positive & ~is_going_up & (x_int == 0) 

92 neg_zero_up = ~is_positive & is_going_up & (x_int == 0x8000) 

93 is_zero_cross = pos_zero_down | neg_zero_up 

94 

95 # IEEE 754: nextafter(NaN, any) = NaN and nextafter(any, NaN) = NaN. 

96 # Return a canonical quiet NaN bit pattern when either operand is NaN; 

97 # this must take precedence over both is_equal and the increments. 

98 # Fold the NaN bit pattern to a compile-time constant so OR-ing it with 

99 # the uint16 tensor does not promote to int32 (see cross_const above). 

100 nan_const: tl.constexpr = exp_mask | 0x0001 # smallest quiet NaN 

101 nan_bits = uint_zero | nan_const 

102 result_int = tl.where( 

103 is_nan, 

104 nan_bits, 

105 tl.where( 

106 is_equal, 

107 x_int, # same value: return input as-is 

108 tl.where(is_zero_cross, x_int + cross_const, x_int + normal_inc), 

109 ), 

110 ) 

111 

112 return result_int.to(input.dtype, bitcast=True) 

113 else: 

114 # float32 

115 return tl_extra_shim.nextafter(input, other)
